children: Memory-chip producer Micron Technology Inc. (MU, Financials) has dropped more than 11% in the previous three months, even as Wall Street remains solidly optimistic on the company.
The average analyst price target is about $1,556.55, implying more than 63% upside from current levels. Micron's broad exposure to the memory cycle is fueling the optimism.

SanDisk is mainly a NAND flash player while Micron sells DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory used in advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems. That gives the company more chances to benefit if tight supply and strong data-center demand keep memory costs elevated.
Analysts expect DRAM prices to climb some 50% this quarter, with NAND prices up about 60%, TipRanks said. The risk is that the same strong pricing environment will draw in more supply.
Chinese memory companies are boosting capacity and an earlier-than-expected ramp up in output could ultimately pressure prices and profits.
That puts Micron in a funny spot for investors. The stock has gained more than 230% this year but analysts see lots of upside.
The next catalyst will be whether memory pricing and HBM demand are enough to justify those projections into Micron's next earnings report.

title: Micron's 11% Drop Hasn't Shaken Wall Street's Bull Case
